title: Agreement without invisible extra work
meaning: Your domestic agreement supports balance when calm participation does not hide additional work already needing shared recognition.
text: You can arrange home through two people’s participation: discussing needs, agreeing times and seeking answers without overlooking the other. The Lovers in the physical position of Muladhara describe this openness in action. Strength in energy tests your footing through excessive containment of dissatisfaction, silently overcoming discomfort. Justice in emotions notices the balance of contribution. Outwardly peaceful agreement can therefore carry an inner account when the same person repeatedly does extra work to preserve the evening, leaving that work unnamed and seemingly included in the previous agreement already.

For example, you agree to cook together, but clearing up quietly falls to one. Asking for help feels awkward because you want to preserve the pleasant result. **Contained disappointment does not make extra work agreed work.** Naming it need not reject participation. Fairness returns to practical arrangements, and peace stops depending on how long someone can bear an unnoticed difference between promised contribution and what actually happens daily.

The difficulty is waiting for effort to be noticed by itself. An account grows, and requests begin only after considerable tiredness. The other may not know how long the difference has been felt. Home supports you more dependably when contributions become visible before resentment accumulates, and clear clarification need not count as disturbing peace already achieved. A shared agreement can include the whole task.
